key_insight: Higher district child poverty is associated with lower access to advanced mathematics, while stronger mathematics preparation is associated with better first-year college grades across nearly every subject.
engineering_relevance: The findings can inform mathematics support and course-design studies for engineering pathways, especially for students entering with weaker preparation.
method: Compare core and advanced course enrollment with district child poverty nationally and in Bexar County.
Link university entrants to sending schools and districts to examine preparation and first-year outcomes.
Compare mathematics section size and unsuccessful outcomes within the same course and term.
evidence_signal: Records from Fall 2014 through Fall 2019 at one broad-access Hispanic-Serving university identify mathematics as the largest single source of unsuccessful course outcomes among entrants who did not return after their first year.
watch_item: These are observational associations, not causal effects; smaller mathematics sections remain a hypothesis requiring a designed study.
paper_title: A Calculus Gradient: Child Poverty, Mathematics Preparation, and First-Year College Performance at a Hispanic-Serving University
